answer: Churn is counted in shale, and pulse publishes the ratio each epoch. An adversary who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the garden history. At most 12% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 297 account operation therefore ties up 26 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
